questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several factors influenced my decision to choose Milan as my Erasmus study destination. First, I was interested in studying in a city with a strong international profile and a high-quality educational environment. Milan is known for its vibrant student life, cultural diversity, and excellent opportunities for both academic and personal development. I was also attracted by the opportunity to experience Italian culture, improve my language skills, and meet people from different countries. In addition, Milan's central location made it easy to travel and explore other parts of Italy and Europe during my stay. Overall, I believed Milan would provide both valuable academic experiences and memorable cultural experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I am extremely satisfied with my Erasmus experience. It has been one of the most rewarding and memorable experiences of my university life. I have not only developed academically but also grown personally by becoming more independent, adaptable, and confident. Living and studying in Milan allowed me to experience a new culture, build friendships with people from all over the world, and create memories that will last a lifetime. I would highly recommend Erasmus to every student, as I truly believe it is one of the best opportunities you can have during your university studies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The university was very helpful and provided clear guidance throughout the entire process. Whenever I had questions, the office responded quickly and were always willing to assist. The information provided before and during my arrival made the transition smooth and helped me settle in without any major difficulties.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to the office at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding housing in Milan was quite challenging, so I would recommend starting the search early and being patient, as it can take some time to find a suitable place. I found my accommodation through
Roofinders.com
, which was helpful in securing a room before my arrival. However, the service is relatively expensive due to additional agency fees. Despite the cost, it provided a safe and reliable way to find accommodation in a competitive housing market.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Housing prices off campus are generally high, so it is important to plan a budget accordingly. You should also be cautious of rental scams. Always verify the landlord or agency, avoid making payments before confirming that the accommodation is legitimate, and use trusted housing platforms whenever possible.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was generally straightforward, but it was different from what I was used to at the UCPH. One of the main challenges was creating my own timetable, as I has to make sure that the courses I wanted to take did not overlap. Finding a combination of cources that fit together required some time and planning. However, once everything was finalised, the process went smoothly, and the university was helpful whenever I had questions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process varied depending on the course. Some courses required registration through the university's online system, while others had to be registered directly with the course professor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office was very helpful, but all of the professor were also very helpful and took their time explaining what we had to do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful. I got all the courses I wanted, which all of my friends also did.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have the opportunity to attend different courses before making your final course selection. I would recommend taking advantage of this by trying out a few different classes to see what genuinely interests you before deciding on your final schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was quit different from UCPH. However, once I got used to the new approach, it was easy to follow the courses and adapt to the academic environment.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, the academic level seemed lower compared to UCPH. There was almost no reading outside of class. However, attending was mandatory for most courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more focused on discussions and presentations, with a strong emphasis on in-class participation. Compared to UCHP, there was very little self-study and independent reading required. Most of the learning took place during classes through discussions, group work, and presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Art and Law
2) Cultural Diversity and Human Rights Law
3) European Labour Law
4) Gender Justice 
5) International Human Rights Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
1) Gender Justice: Professor Nardocci was very passionate, which was clearly reflected in her teaching. Her enthusiasm made the classes engaging and interesting. In addition, she was very helpful and provided guidance regarding my studies in Denmark. 
2) International Human Rights Law: Easy multiple-questions exam with two open questions, and professor Grassi was very sweet and helpful. 
3) Cultural Diversity and Human Rights Law: Interesting class, but the professor was not that helpful.

questions.answer: The rent was more expensive. Travelling around Italy was less expensive, as I used Flixbus and found cheap tickets.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many activities and events available to participate in, especially if you became a member of the ESN group. The group organised different social events and activities, which made it easier to meet other exchange students and become part of the international community.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Museum visits and sports activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend using the weekends to explore other cities in Italy. I planned my schedule so that I did not have any classes on Fridays, which gave me a longer weekend and the opportunity to travel more and stay overnight in different places. It was a great way to experience more of Italy and make the most of my time abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. A great city for exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and socialise with your Italian classmates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The more relaxed way of living. Their way of enjoying life at a slower pace. Very different from Denmark. Italy taught me to be more present and appreciate the small things in everyday life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start your housing search early and be careful with scams. 
2. Take advantage of the flexibility during your exchange. Try different courses before making your final choices. Plan your schedule wisely, for example by keeping some days free, so you have time to explore Milan and Italy.
3. Be open-minded and embrace the Italian lifestyle.

questions.answer: The many friendships I made with people from different backgrounds and cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing.
